Answer FOUR questions. All questions carry equal marks.

INSTRUCTIONS

1. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

2. The use of SIMPLE electronic calculator is allowed.

3. Show clear working in your answer booklet where necessary.

Sujet scanné de 2 pages (page de garde, puis les questions 1 à 6 sur une seule page) lu en image ; l'en-tête publicitaire du site et le filigrane (gcerevision.com) sont ignorés. Points : pour chaque question les points imprimés totalisent 20, conformément à « All questions carry equal marks » : aucun écart. Coquilles du sujet imprimé recopiées telles quelles dans les énoncés (« Give briefly explain FIVE functions », « outline » sans majuscule en 5(c) et 6(b), « Containerization ») : elles ne changent pas le sens de la question.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give any **FIVE** advantages of each of the following:

(i) Containerization, and

(ii) Pipeline transport.

(10 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Advantages of containerization (any five, 5 marks)**

**Containerization** is the transport of goods packed inside large standard-size steel boxes (containers) that are sealed at the point of departure and moved by ship, truck or train.

1. **Less damage and theft.** Goods are sealed in a strong box and handled as a single unit, so they are less likely to be broken, stolen or spoilt by weather.
2. **Faster loading and unloading.** Cranes lift whole containers, so ships spend less time in port and turn round quickly.
3. **Lower packing cost.** Goods need lighter packing, which reduces packaging costs.
4. **Lower insurance premiums**, because the risk of damage and theft is smaller.
5. **Door-to-door service.** The same container can move from the factory to the customer by road, rail and sea without being opened, so goods do not have to be unpacked and repacked at each stage.
6. **Efficient use of space.** The standard size allows containers to be stacked in ships, ports and yards.

**(ii) Advantages of pipeline transport (any five, 5 marks)**

**Pipeline transport** is the movement of liquids and gases such as crude oil, natural gas and water through underground or overground pipes.

1. **Low running cost.** After the pipeline has been built, the cost per unit moved is low and little labour is needed.
2. **Continuous flow, day and night.** The movement does not stop, so supplies are regular.
3. **Safe and secure.** There is little loss from theft and little risk of accidents on the road, since the product stays inside the pipe.
4. **Not affected by traffic congestion** or bad roads, and **little effect of the weather** if pipes are underground.
5. **Reliable and no empty return journeys**, as there is no vehicle to be sent back.
6. **Reduces road traffic and pollution**, and so lowers the damage to roads.

(Any five points for each part are enough.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
State **SIX** facilities of a modern airport

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A modern airport has the following facilities.

1. **Runways, taxiways and aprons** on which aircraft take off, land, move and park.
2. **Control tower and air traffic control equipment** (radar and radio) to guide the aircraft safely.
3. **Passenger terminal buildings** with check-in desks, waiting lounges and boarding gates.
4. **Customs, immigration and health control posts** to check passengers, baggage and goods.
5. **Cargo terminals and warehouses** for the loading, storage and handling of freight.
6. **Baggage handling systems** and security screening equipment.
7. **Hangars and maintenance workshops** for the repair and servicing of aircraft, and **fuel supply**.
8. **Services to passengers**: banks and bureaux de change, shops, restaurants, car parks, and taxi and bus services.
9. **Fire-fighting and medical (first-aid) services.**

(Any six facilities are enough.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
outline **FOUR** reasons why a firm may own its private fleet of distribution vehicles.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A firm may own its own fleet of distribution vehicles for the following reasons.

1. **Control over deliveries.** The firm decides when and where to deliver, so goods reach customers on time and at the time the firm chooses.
2. **Advertising.** The vehicles carry the name, logo and slogan of the firm, which advertises it wherever they go.
3. **Suitable vehicles.** The firm can buy vehicles that are designed for its goods (for example refrigerated trucks for frozen foods), which reduces damage.
4. **Better customer service and flexibility.** Delivery can be arranged at short notice and urgent orders can be met, and drivers who know the products and customers can build goodwill.
5. **Lower cost in the long run** for a firm that makes frequent deliveries, compared with paying a transport company each time.

(Any four reasons are enough.)
